findings.evidence: Specialization.lean:115-128 obtains `v` from `exists_right_inv` and proves `heval : eval u * eval v = 1`, exactly the `hfg`/`hmul` steps of IntegralCoefficients.lean:125-127; the `le_antisymm` branches use only `norm_mul_le_of_le` (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Ring/Basic.lean:223) and `norm_evalIntSeries_le_one`, never that `q` is a unit.
findings.fix: Add `norm_mul_evalIntSeries_of_isUnit (x : K) {f : ℤ⟦X⟧} (hf : IsUnit f) : ‖x * evalIntSeries q hq f‖ = ‖x‖` in IntegralCoefficients.lean next to `norm_evalIntSeries_le_one`, with the `le_antisymm` argument (nothing in it uses `x = q`), derive `norm_evalIntSeries_eq_one_of_isUnit` from it at `x = 1` via `one_mul`/`norm_one`, and reduce `norm_tateCurveAt_Δ` to `rw [tateCurveAt, WeierstrassCurve.map_Δ, hΔ, map_mul, evalIntSeries_X]` plus that lemma. While moving it, replace `simpa using norm_mul_le_of_le (le_refl _) …` with an explicit `(norm_mul_le_of_le le_rfl h).trans_eq (mul_one _)` and `simp [mul_assoc, heval]` with `rw [mul_assoc, heval, mul_one]`, so the bound does not depend on the default simp set.
findings.issue: The 12-line proof inlines a general fact — for `IsUnit f`, `‖x * evalIntSeries q hq f‖ = ‖x‖` for every `x`, valid for submultiplicative norms — and re-derives the right inverse plus the two-sided bound already done in `norm_evalIntSeries_eq_one_of_isUnit` (IntegralCoefficients.lean:121-134), which the PR leaves with no remaining users (grep finds references only inside its own file).

summary: The generalized `norm_tateCurveAt_Δ` inlines the reusable fact that multiplying by the evaluation of a formal unit preserves the norm under a merely submultiplicative norm, duplicating the inverse-extraction argument of the existing `norm_evalIntSeries_eq_one_of_isUnit` (which the PR simultaneously leaves with no users). The coefficient proofs via `congrArg`/evaluation are a clear improvement.
